utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Our next witness is General Dragan Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud the words that have been shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You will now be examined by Mr. Cepic on behalf of Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: For the record, please, your full name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Zivanovic, son of Milovan.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Date and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 8th of January, 1955, the village of Ba, municipality of Ljig Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please tell me what schooling you attended.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Military secondary school, military academy, up to the School of National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What were the most important posts you held in your military service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: From platoon commander to corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In 1998 and 1999, what were the posts that you held?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 until mid-June I was Chief of Staff in the command of the 125th Motorised Brigade, and then from mid-June onwards I was commander of the 125th Motorised Brigade of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, what was the situation like in the spring of 1998? Can you hear?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't hear anything, but that's fine. I can hear you from the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you hear now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: A bit better.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you like the volume to be put up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because I have trouble hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is it better now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, spring of 1998, what was the security situation in the territory of Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was at risk due to the terrorist activities of the terrorist Siptar forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In that period of time, in the spring of 1998, were there terrorist attacks on the forces of the Army of Yugoslavia as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They started attacking the army forces by crossing the state border with Albania, attacking border forces, and the forces of my unit, 125th Motorised Brigade, were first attacked on the 23rd of May, 1998, on the road Djakovica-Smonica- Ponosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, would you please tell us, where were the strongholds of terrorist forces in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The strongest terrorist bases were in the villages of the Jablanica region, Glodjane, Rznic, Saptej, Gramocelj and other villages in that area and also in the Reka region and in the villages around Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What was the situation in the northern part of that is to say Drenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The situation was more grave there. The first emergence of terrorism was in the Drenica region. It is now ten years that this happened, namely, the first attack was around the Orthodox new year in the sector of the Pec monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, in the 1998 period, what were the main tasks of your brigade? When I say "your brigade," I'm referring to the 125th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The main tasks of the 125th Motorised Brigade were, first of all, regular combat training; protection of personnel and materiel and equipment; third, intensified protection of state border in depth; the fourth task was to protect the roads when there were military movements on the roads; and the fifth task was to support MUP forces in some of the actions in the second part of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You mentioned protection of state border in depth and the fact that the roads were at risk. Would you please tell us what was the situation like regarding these two aspects?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There were intensified illegal crossings of the border from Kosovo and Metohija into the Republic of Albania. They armed themselves there, and then they illegally crossed the border back, terrorists and armed forces, armed persons, going back to Metohija, and by doing so they created conditions necessary to arm terrorist forces. As for the roads, the most endangered road was Kosovska Mitrovica-Pec road over or via Rudnik, then Pec-Decani-Djakovica road, especially in the area between Decani and Djakovica, and Pec-Pristina road in the sector Glina-Kijevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Tell me something about the combat training of soldiers in that period leading up to the beginning of the war. How was it conducted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was conducted just like in the previous period. It was conducted in the exercise manoeuvre grounds according to the curriculum for training units and soldiers. In the time-period leading up to the war it was conducted under very difficult circumstances due to terrorist forces that were located nearby and that were attacking, daily attacking members of the Ministry of the Interior and army servicemen. This put at risk the people who were in charge of the training.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have certain documents concerning the method and extent of this training. These documents have not been translated yet, and we will ask that they be admitted into evidence at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, we had some evidence here during the Prosecution case where we heard that the military forces during that period of time while the OSCE mission stayed in Kosovo and Metohija conducted extensive military manoeuvres. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not true. On a monthly basis according to our regular plan for combat training, our brigade was supposed to have at least, or rather, at least 30 training exercises at the level of a company. However, we were able to implement only four to five trainings at the level of a platoon, which is to say 100 to 120 people. These are no manoeuvres.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, units of the 125th Motorised Brigade and their servicemen, were they aware of the regulations and provisions of the international law and international humanitarian law and international laws of war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, every soldier received his own pocket-sized copy. We also received orders from superior command and we drafted our own orders aimed at preventive action to ensure that these provisions would be complied with and to ensure that civilians and others would not be endangered and put at risk.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, in the fall of 1998 did the command of the Pristina Corps also conduct some training courses devoted to this topic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had some seminars, and I sent two or three officers to attend the seminars, and after they return they came back, they conveyed it to us, and we presented it to our units.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see Exhibit 5D755.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's just what I told you about, the two people that I sent to attend this training seminar.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So is this the document that confirms what you told us previously?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. For the sake of the record, is this a document coming from your brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it says so in the heading, 125th Motorised Brigade, 26 October 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see Exhibit P1642.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting -- I think it will come up soon. Yes, that's right. We see a document from 1998 here. This is a document of the 125th Brigade. Do you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I see the first three items.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, what was the attitude towards foreign representatives and diplomats, or rather, was there any concern for their security; and if so, how were these measures implemented? Was this concern a real one or did you just pretend to be concerned for their safety?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The corps commander was constantly required to devote the utmost attention to the protection of civilians so that when we responded to the fire opened at us by terrorist Siptar forces, we wouldn't hurt civilians especially if in the vicinity of terrorists there were foreign representatives. We had to be very careful in opening fire so that we wouldn't inflict any injuries or hurt anybody because we were responsible for them while they were located in our country.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, we spoke of terrorist attacks. In the fall of 1998, did you perhaps uncover some traces of particularly grave crimes committed by terrorists?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In October my reconnaissance people in the Volujak sector found a cave where they found some remains, or rather, some bones.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what happened subsequently with the exhumed bodies after 2000? Do you know from the media what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that the corps commander sent a team to investigate this together with the MUP organs. I think that it was in February or March of 1999, and as for the media I learned from the media that exhumations had been carried out I think in 2005 and that some 30 bodies of Serbs who had been killed were found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in order to speed up this examination, document of the 125th Brigade PD747 [as interpreted] speaks of this. I hope that Mr. Hannis does not mind that we're not going to bring it up. 5D747. We can see the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does this document tell us how these people died?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Or where they died?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that would be the best solution to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you please tell us. Does it solve the problem of how or where they died; and if it doesn't, what's the point?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: They just found the bones and in 2005 those bones and additional bones they buried in Belgrade and UN mission sent experts in that location, and they found that those bones and bodies are from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, I understand that, but how does that help us unless we know how they died and where they died.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: They are from Orahovac. We have some additional documents which will confirm that those bodies and the rest of bodies, actually, are from the people from Orahovac --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's what I'm trying to understand from you. We don't want an accumulation of evidence about dead bodies with nothing that explains to us what happened to them. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's my objection from the document that I had seen there was nothing to tie it to anything in our case. That's why I had a foundational objection and a relevance objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it looks as though Mr. Cepic is going to supplement the material to give some indication of that. When were you proposing to do that, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: As soon as I finish with couple next witnesses, Your Honour, and I have to request some additional material. I have good communication with the UN mission in Kosovo right now, and I hope that I will receive something more in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The further we get in the case the more possible it should be to focus your evidence on the issues that are really concerning us. And at first blush this does not seem to be one of them, but please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we see on our screens 5D747.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this a document from your brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And does this same confirm that remains were found, remains of bodies in that area that we were discussing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You can see here based on the entry and exit wounds on the victims that they were killed by a shot to the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we see exhibit number 5D1241, please. This is a video material and my assistant will play now with your leave, Your Honour, if you allow us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe this is -- if he's playing the entire video or if this is one part -- we've got multiple segments for the same exhibit I have the same problem that's been raised before that we need some way to identify what particular segment we're referring to that's the exhibit that's being addressed now. I know there was a recent filing about this by the Lazarevic Defence, but I don't think it adequately addressed the problem. We need to identify it some way, as it's minute 1, 30 seconds to minute 2, 30 seconds, some way that somebody picking up the record later on is going to be able to match it up with what's in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The issue arising from the last one is being addressed, as you probably know. What is the position with this video, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just one second, Your Honour, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This is the video clip which title is: "Village Volujak, or Celo Volujak, and we would like to play from 30 seconds until the 1 minute and 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's all that is being played from this video, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Single clip?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And -- I'm sorry, may I say, and with your leave later on some other video clip not in relation to Volujak but in relation to something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But separate from this and therefore clearly identifiable as something different, so please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What should we with be looking for here? It's silent --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Cave Volujak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What am I looking for?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we just -- we just showing the material in relation about General testified, and we saw one soldier -- actually one officer VJ on that position. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, can you please explain what this footage is about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is footage of the cave where my soldiers and officers found remains in October 1998, and you can see the remains of the bodies and the skulls. On behalf of my command Lieutenant-Colonel, later he became a Colonel, Dragan Petrovic was the engineering chief in the 125th Brigade. He was there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Sir, can you please tell me this, we're moving to another topic now. Can you tell me what your cooperation was like with the OSCE mission members during their stay in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Cooperation was in the spirit of the order from the General Staff via the 3rd Army and the Pristina Corps commander. We directly corresponded - let me put it that way - and talked via the liaison officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have on our screens documents 5D773, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me look at the signature, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask, is there an English translation for this document? I haven't seen one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately we haven't received translation for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Too many documents we requested translation for, too many documents, but I can -- with your leave I can request admission of this document later on on bar table, and we can read -- and if you allow me, the witness can read just a part of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's my objection, Your Honour. I don't mind him filing a bar table objection -- a motion later or I don't mind him asking the witness if that's his signature for purposes of authentication, but I do mind him asking him to comment or read on part of it when I can't see it in English and know what the whole document is because it limits my ability to cross-examine while the witness is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is quite a short document, Mr. Hannis. Now, I appreciate that you may have a more general objection because of the number of documents that you face and it may be that this is not the best example, I don't know; but is this one we could deal with here without setting a precedent that -- you might regard as unfortunate or is this one that you really seriously feel could cause you prejudice if we proceeded the way Mr. Cepic suggests?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, judging by the date I don't think it's going to cause me a serious problem and I hope by now you realize I'm a pretty agreeable guy on these things. I'm willing to do that. But I don't want to set a precedent and I don't want this to be the first of 50 exhibits with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thanks. Mr. Cepic, I know that there was an exchange of e-mails about the problem of untranslated exhibits for this witness and that you have been taking steps to address that issue as best you can. And we note that one of the ways of doing so is to seek admission of documents from the bar table in due course and to exercise restraint in court in the way in which you're using the documents. So we'll allow you to use this one the way you suggest, but that should be no -- taken as no real guide as to what we will do in relation to others as you proceed if it's clear that there is a large number or that the individual documents call -- create a real risk of prejudice to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if I may make one request. When future exhibits are being presented if Mr. Cepic knows there's not a translation if he can indicate that. It saves me trying to look through and double-check and maybe being late in raising an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It looks as though he didn't know about this one though, Mr. Hannis, albeit he is aware of the problem in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, my colleagues are anxious that we should make it clear to you that we are extremely concerned about the absence of English translations for documents and that we will not necessarily by any means follow the course of action that we're following with this document as we progress if we see that there's a real issue building up, either in individual circumstances affecting Prosecution or in general affecting the conduct of the case. Meanwhile, this one will be marked for identification in the usual way, and you may proceed to deal with it by inviting the witness to read some part of it that you wish to deal with at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, just briefly, you see the document in front of you. Is this your signature in lower right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please read the introductory part of the document and tell us what this document is asking.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: "On the basis of the order of the command of the Pristina command, confidential number 1468-1, dated 27th of October, 1998, and for the purpose of implementing the agreement with the OSCE and NATO mission for verification in Kosovo and Metohija and in accordance with the Security Council Resolution 1199, I order ..." This is the preamble of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In order not to read everything, can you please just read paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: "1. I appoint the following senior officers as liaison officers with the OSCE mission: The Kosovska Mitrovica and Vucitrn garrisons Major Momcilo Vojnovic, chief of the intelligence section; and his deputy would be Major Dragan Trifunovic. Pec garrison Captain First Class Aca Cubranovic and his deputy would be Captain Dragan Branovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. And the representatives of the mission, did they monitor or inspect the weaponry in your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 5D326, 5D327, 328, 329, and 5D330. They are documents that confirms that the representatives from mission verified the weapons in the 125th Brigade, and I would like to request their admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And there are translations into English of all of these, are there?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I thought it is not necessarily because the documents are half in Serbian, half in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, you mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We can tender -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The terms of the documents already exist in both languages, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, these will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, did you personally participate in meetings with the mission representatives?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did while the Deputy Planque from France was still there and he was succeeded by Leif Widmar [phoen] from Sweden.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... translated that is 5D27 and that document confirms the presence of General during the meeting with representatives from the OSCE. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, did the mission representatives attend the exercises and training and target practice executed by members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, since we were obliged to announce these exercises in advance, they did attend the exercises, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 5D23, 25, and 50. All three documents are translated and confirms the previous words of General. Thank you, Your Honour. Could we see on our screens 5D49, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime while we're waiting for the document, General, were there any attacks on the OSCE mission members in that period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recall there were attacks in the sector of a village close to Decani, it's the village of Lumbardja, and this was in mid-May 1999 -- in mid-January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two members were attacked, I believe they were from Scotland, one of them was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Attacked the wrong people there, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, does this document confirm your evidence and is this a document from your brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, in early January, or rather, in January of 1999 there was an action called sword or "Mac." What was its meaning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Eight soldiers were kidnapped from the 125th Motorised Brigade in the Bajgora sector, and then the terrorists refused to release them. So from the 3rd Army down to the corps and down to my brigade, I received an order to engage units in order to rescue these soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we see document P1160, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Does it confirm your earlier testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This has to do with the disengagement of these forces from the 16th of January onwards. After the soldiers were released they came back to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What does it mean "disengagement"? Had there been an action carried out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not at all, no action.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the army perhaps praised for not acting, for restraint?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was told that the army was praised and I was told so through the documents and even by the OSCE president at the time, Mr. Knut Vollebaek.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: There is already in e-court system Exhibit 2D181 which confirms those words.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, let us briefly, or rather, we're still in January 1999. Your combat group which was in the broader Junik sector, did you receive a visit by members of the mission, those who were involved in the protection of the state border in depth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did receive a visit, I think at one point even Colonel Ciaglinski came to visit us.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were there any local residents there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly there were. I think that he even spoke to local residents. He asked them whether they had any problems due to the army presence, and they told him that they had no problems with the army whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in B/C/S third page, in English ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, the transcript didn't pick up the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: 5D648, please. In B/C/S third page -- just the first page for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, whose document is this? Would you please look at it, at the heading.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the document of the command of the 3rd Army liaison team, mission liaison team. If I'm not mistaken, it was headed by General Toma Mladenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we have in e-court third page in B/C/S and third page in English also this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see the second paragraph in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, have you seen the last paragraph of this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. It says here: "On the 24th of January," and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You don't need to read this. Does this confirm your words?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we now have 5D1178.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just to be clear, which paragraph does that reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Second paragraph in English on the third page, Your Honour, which is between 1730 and 18 hours a meeting was held between mission representative --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. It was your reference to the 24th of January I wasn't clear about. Is this just at the end?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I didn't mention the date, but the document is probably from that date or for that period, that week, and during the -- during the testifying of Mr. Ciaglinski he confirmed that he was in Junik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, the problem though is, though, Mr. Cepic, you directed attention to the second paragraph in English. The witness was dealing with the third paragraph in English, he was dealing with the one about between 8.30 and 9.00 on the 24th. So let's be clear what it is he's actually speaking to -- speaking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, would you please look at penultimate and ultimate paragraph in the Serbian version, the document you see on the right. Would you please tell me the last paragraph in Serbian, what does it discuss?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Shall I read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You don't need to read it. Just look at it and then move on to page 4 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Does it confirm your testimony concerning this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: End of page 3, beginning of page 4?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did Colonel Ciaglinski speak to the civilians in the Junik sector?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, with a group of local residents, Siptars, as it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It is the third paragraph in English, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have now 5D1178. I'm afraid we haven't got translation of this document yet. I already spoke to Mr. Hannis in relation to this document because this document is related to something else which I would like to clarify with next few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've managed to keep Mr. Hannis -- no you haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we did talk about some documents. I'm not sure, is this one that refers to Kosare? I see an affirmative nod. I don't have an objection to him speaking about this one and having it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I clearly clarified to my learned friend that this document is in relation to document -- Prosecutor's Exhibit P2808. This is the order from Pristina Corps from February which number is 455-1, very important document; and I would like to clarify something with this witness, Your Honour. And I think that I clarified to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't have a problem with that, Your Honour, but I don't want the document admitted until I've seen it in English and have a chance to deal with it in writing if need be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What you're saying in relation to this one is a bit different from the earlier one, that you're saying not only should this be marked for identification, but it shouldn't be admitted except by way of a bar table motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I would like to see the English and maybe I won't have any objections, it can be admitted without him making a further submission because I can see how it's relevant and I have no concerns about authenticity or anything else. Am I making life more complicated than it needs to be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think it's important to have a scheme that everyone's clear about, and this document, Mr. Cepic, should be the subject of a bar table motion, unless you are able to reach agreement with Mr. Hannis for its admission. So once you've got the translation, if you can reach agreement with him, then you can submit it -- you can file it on the basis of an agreed -- on an agreed basis, but failing that you would have to support it with other submissions. Meanwhile, it will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With your leave I would like to ask some questions in relation to mentioned document, not precisely about document but in relation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, during proofing I showed you a document of the Pristina Corps marked in e-court as P2808, which is an order to crush Siptar terrorist forces in the Mala Drenica region. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, I think the date was the 16th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Did you produce your own order based on that order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, and that was done in accordance with the order of the corps, and that was the last group training, which is to say the training of the command of the 125th Motorised Brigade in order to prepare officers and develop plans for future action.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, was that order carried out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, because this involved group training. This was placed in archives and used for training purposes. It was not carried out, not implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like to see a video clip in e-court which is 5D1241, the title of the material: "The village of Prekaze and the anniversary or commemoration there." Could we please play it from the 017 to 1.21. The witness will explain what this discusses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it the same -- are we still dealing with the same issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Different topic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Different, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this footage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. This is the celebration of the anniversary of the founding of the so-called KLA in the village of Prekaze and the celebration dedicated to the Jashari brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When did this take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the first half of March 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of this gathering?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew about it via the Ministry of the Interior and by my people, officers, who were involved in operative work.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was anything done against these KLA forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Our hands were tied due to the presence of a large number of civilians and because the OSCE monitors were there as well. Also because my commander did not allow me to do anything. He actually warned me several times on that day and in the preceding days.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Following this celebration, how did the situation unfold in the Drenica region?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Following this the intensity of the attacks of Siptar terrorist forces on the members of MUP and the army increased. Practically speaking, the units of the 125th Brigade in the sector of Kosovska Mitrovica and Vucitrn were practically encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, March, was it imminent that there would be a NATO aggression?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when did your units leave the barracks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just before the aggression. The only people who remained there were those who secured the barracks and other facilities, that is to say guards remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What sectors did you take up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: With our combat units I took up the sectors outside of residential areas, and in town there remained only a part of the command and logistics in order to carry out mobilisation and provide logistical support.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 08, please. 708. We have translation in English also.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir, is this your order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What are you requesting here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the case of air-strikes we should take up the following sectors and axes in order to prevent the enemy from penetrating any further, the enemy or any other elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, sir, in this courtroom we heard the evidence of Witness Mahmut Selimi [as interpreted], who claimed to have seen military forces, among others, in sectors to the west of Kosovska Mitrovica near the villages of Tamnik, Zabare, Sipolje, Suvi Do. What about the forces of the 125th Brigade, were they in that sector too?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tamnik, Zabare, Suvi Do, no never. My own elements that the area on the 8th of April, 1999, therefore they couldn't possibly have been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any check-points in that area or the broader area, if you like, the military, did the military have any check-points?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I had no check-points in that sector not at any point in time throughout the war. I had two mixed check-points or combined check-points one in the Ibarska Slatina area; it's on the road from Kosovo Mitrovica to Leposavic and the other was at Savine Vode. The one at Leposavic or Ibarska Slatina was abandoned by my forces in late April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the task of the military at those check-points?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Simply to inspect any military traffic, motor vehicles and those walking, and also to check anyone crossing in a VJ uniform whether they were making any legal crossing or illegal one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 09, please. 709, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir, is this your order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have -- could we scroll down in B/C/S and also in English I need the count 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir, would you please have a look at item 1, item 2, and item 3. Tell us, what was the main task at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The main task at the time was to prevent any incursions from the Republic of Albania by NATO forces. The task was to block these roads and to organize groups that would carry this out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. During our proofing session --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... P1968.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, did you ever receive this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In addition to this one, did you receive any other orders with a header that read: "Joint Command for KiM"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, several others that had to do with the involvement of my forces lending support to the MUP forces. The last one I received was on the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In what way did you receive these orders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The same way as any other, in an envelope. This was just before the war broke out so there was a signalsman from the Pristina Corps who was involved. I dispatched him and I got this in an envelope along with a number of other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, what did this mean to you, a document like this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: To me this was a document produced by the corps command detailing coordination and the involvement of my forces, some units of my forces, that were to lend support to the MUP forces in a certain sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, did such a thing as a Joint Command exist for you as a command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was no such thing as a Joint Command. This was some sort of a coordination plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, who was your direct superior throughout 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Pristina Corps commander, General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you sent reports, who would you send them to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was always the corps command that I submitted my reports to. Whenever there was something important, an important report, I would send it directly to the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have count 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How many pages are on this document, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Six pages, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we go to the end of it, please. Is there no indication of who it was sent to on the document, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I don't see, Your Honour. If you allow me to say but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, this document is in the form in which you received it, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Unsigned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: With no indication that it was to be addressed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's true in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was this the first time you had received such a document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When did you receive the first document in this form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think in July 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How did you know what you were supposed to do with such documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I used our communications system to call the commander, but he was away and then his operative explained to me that this document was all right and that this was about coordination, about coordinated action, about coordinating support for the MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The commander at that time would be a different commander from the one who was responsible for this particular document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who the commander was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but we have wrong translation in B/C/S because in your question was not the word "MUP," and in the answer of the witness the witness answered in relation to MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, the answer makes sense certainly in English in relation to the question, but I'm trying to be clear about the situation in 1998 in July when this first happened and March, which is the date of the one we're looking at. The commander was a different commander in March from the commander in July, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the commander of the Pristina Corps - and this is how it continued, and this was a document produced by the Pristina Corps command, and that was always my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But just deal with my question. In July 1998 the commander of the Pristina Corps was General Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And in March 1999 the commander was General Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Two different people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you recollect how many of these Joint Command documents were actually signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometime in March 1999. It was some sort of an amendment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, let us please just look at what should be page 3 in the B/C/S, item 5.2. You see what the tasks were for the 125 Brigade, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that item 5.2 I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you draw this line for me on a map, how far you got during this action in terms of lending support?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I should, although I'm not such a good draftsman since I've been away from work for quite some time now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm sorry, 5D1389.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, it's in black and white.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Mr. Cepic please be asked to speak up a little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, there's a problem for the interpreters hearing you because of the position of the microphone I think. Just make sure you're speaking into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise to interpreters. I'll try to avoid that problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir, is this a good map for you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you were just telling me what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Use red to mark your own moves. Tell me if you encountered any resistance and then later use blue to mark the terrorist forces and please mark the point which you reached in this action, that is essential.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This was the initial position for one of the groups, that is where they started out from, and this is where another group started out from. This group arrived just outside this village. I will do a dotted line here to mark how far we got, and then I'll draw this at an angle or I'll do a wedge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're certainly the best we've had so far at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The General was the professor on military academy, so ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the two groups that were on their way and they got as far as this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Use the blue pen now, please, and show me where the terrorist forces were.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the so-called Cubrelj, that's where they were, all over here, Rakitnica. And then above Srbica, Lausa. This is Lausa right here, and Sakutu Puta [phoen], and then here between the village of Krusevac and Lausa there was a thickly wooded area Baljak [phoen] and along the road to Turicevac and Tusilje, the Lausa, or rather, the Devic forest. And then Rezala, one of the strongest positions, best strongholds, and then the whole of this area I'm not drawing this now: Izbica, Brocrna Vocnjak, Kladernica, Citak, Citacko, Leocina, and all that and all this entire area all the way up to this area over here, Josanica and where all the other forces were going. That's as far as I remember. It goes without saying the adjacent unit here in Makrmal and Likovac and other notorious terrorist strongholds, Gornje and Donje Obrinje. Just as well, so much for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, the line that you've just drawn for us, did you move any further from this line, your forces, for the purposes of the record?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, our forces went no further than this. Once they'd reached this line they returned to where they'd started out from in Gornja Klina and then the turn-off to Srbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. All right. This is what I want to know now --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have an IC number for this document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC164, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, OTP Witness Mehmet Mazrekaj testified in this courtroom before this Trial Chamber saying that sometime in late March in the village of Pozar the KLA killed 18 soldiers. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did a clash occur in late March with the KLA forces in that area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 29th of March, we lent support to the MUP forces in the Pozar village area. We actually dispatched three tanks over there to that area. During the fighting a tank was hit by an Armbrust from the rear in the Pozar village area destroying that tank and one of my soldiers were killed, Private Dunic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, have we now moved to a different subject? Please don't move that IC document that was on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've moved away from that. I don't want to interrupt what you're doing but there's a couple of matters arise in relation to the drawing on the map if we could have it returned to the screen. On this you've marked a large number of KLA positions. What strength were they therein compared with the strength of your forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The total of their forces outnumbered ours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And how many troops did you have engaged in this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My two combat groups numbered 350 men. We were lending support to the MUP units and they had as many people as we did; therefore, the total was about 700 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How was it that you lent support to them? What did you actually do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we say "support," we mean support by manoeuvring, in this case combat units, combat equipment, or firing. We would take up some prominent features and facilities. We would protect any advances that they made, we would secure their flanks and try to attack the firing positions of the terrorist forces wherever we believed that the MUP units alone would not have been successful in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could I change the topic? Thank you. Actually, to return to previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, we talked about the village of Pozar, how that tank was destroyed and one of the soldiers killed. What about your forces were they in the village of Belik [phoen] on the previous day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, Witness Mazrekaj said that there was a column of civilians moving at the time, and the column was led by two police APCs and a military one as well. Do you think that would have been possible?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No that would not have been possible. I did not have a single APC in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Witness Edison Zatriqi says that the Carsija mosque and the other mosque in Kapesnica were destroyed. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that and those certainly weren't my units operating there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This same witness claims that on the 27th of March, 1999, in Pec the army started shelling from the hospital yard and the secondary school-yard. They were firing at Kapesnica village, and he says he actually saw this. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's not true. I never used the hospital or anything like that, any facility like that, a school, for example, for military purposes and as a place to fire from. In the hospital itself there was an element from the medical corps that was stationed there. We provided medical assistance to the population as well, Albanian and Serb alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about the medical corps, General, is that a combat unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it's a logistical unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, sir, were your forces involved in the Jablanica action early April 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were lending support to the MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have P2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about your activities, were they based on this document we see now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have on our screens 5D465, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this your combat report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see the date, it's two days after that order. Can you please look at item 2.1, Combat Group 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It says here that pursuant to a decision of the commander they took a certain sector. Which decision of the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The decision of the Pristina Corps commander that we showed a while ago dated the 2nd of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who is this report to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Pristina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The -- what is the number of the 2nd April order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, we have to have a break at this stage, that will be for about 20 minutes. Could you leave the courtroom with the usher while we have this break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we shall resume at five past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, in my speed I omitted to ask you something, and that has to do with the village of Bukos, which is mentioned on a number of occasions in this courtroom and this is also relating to the winter 1999 period just before the war. General, sir, are you aware that representatives of the OSCE mission erroneously reported about the situation in the village of Bukos?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, document 5D26 has already been admitted, that relates to that, and I would like to show the witness document 5D653 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, are you aware that because of this erroneous reporting on the situation in the village of Bukos any representative of the OSCE mission was replaced?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was informed about this by the person in charge of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We're just waiting for the document in B/C/S. Can you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There must be a translation problem there. Who informed you about this, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The leader of the mission liaison team, Colonel Kotur from the Pristina Corps informed me about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, do you see the upper left-hand corner of the document? Can you please tell me whose document this is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is also a document by the 3rd Army command and this is the mission's liaison team that was still headed by General Mladenovic if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in B/C/S and also in English. In B/C/S is it possible to scroll down, please, and to zoom in, please, the paragraph before the last one. And in English that is the paragraph -- the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir, what is stated in this document, does this confirm what you have just said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now I'm going to go back to the war time-period. General, did you receive an order to break-up and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces in the region of Rugovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: For clarity, this is 1878, that's how it's marked in e-court, D. This is another document with a heading "Joint Command." General, sir, will you please tell me --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have that document on our screens, please. P1878, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is P1878?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could we have second page, bottom of the page in B/C/S -- actually, count 5, 5.1. Could we scroll down in B/C/S, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see the very end of the page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, our assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, did you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And was this assignment carried out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We will continue. Can you please tell me -- well, we've seen some actions where you provided support for the MUP forces. What I'm interested in is what was the size of the force from the brigade that was engaged on average and where was the bulk of your forces in that period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The bulk of my forces was securing the state border, and the part of the brigade that was engaged to support MUP depended on the situation but it went up to 50 [as interpreted] per cent of my overall force.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we have mistake in transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat the percentage.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Earlier we saw in this order that a battalion that was resubordinated to you from the 58th Brigade was supposed to carry out an assignment in the Rugovska Klisora. Can you please tell me where that battalion was located earlier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the 2nd Light Infantry Battalion without any heavy weapons, and it was located on the line, mostly the line of blockade, where it was ordered to be. I ordered it to be there for purposes of defence, and this corresponded to the line of blockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, you said that the bulk of your forces was securing the state border. What I'm interested is this: Was this any significant or exceptionally significant attack on the state border and the sovereignty of our country?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 9th of April, 1999, at -- on Easter or during Easter this attack did take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what that was all about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This had to do -- it was a classic air and land fight under the name of Strela Jedan where the Albanian forces were engaged, also terrorist forces that had left Kosovo and Metohija, and they had the support of logistical forces that were in the depth of our territory, or rather, Jablanica, Reka, Djakovica, Decani, and with the support of NATO air force, they enjoyed the support of the NATO air force.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at exhibit 5D4568 [as interpreted], please. 5D468.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, is this a report by your brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And paragraphs marked 1 -- well, actually, can you tell us what paragraph 1 is about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It talks about a breakthrough on the axis of Kosare by land forces from the Republic of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We can see the last sentence where it says that there is also a possibility that there are Mujahedin among the Siptar terrorist forces. Did you have any information about this, about the presence of Mujahedin among the terrorist forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, later we did have information about that even one of the terrorists who was killed then happened to be a black man.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at Exhibit 5D166 -- 1266 in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this another report on the same subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, that is the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Does this one deal with the air support question, the one that's in front of us? Does it tell us what the NATO were actually doing?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I can clarify with the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, sir, can you please explain in paragraph 1 where it says that passage should be ensured for the NATO ground forces --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I understand that. What I'm anxious to find out is where there's reference to what was happening in the air, because the witness told us that this was a classic battle involving land confrontation with air support. So can we see where the battle -- where the combat report deals with the -- what was happening in the air, please. Can you help us with that, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see the end and I don't know what exactly it says there, Your Honour, but probably there are other reports that talk about actions on the Planik-Ponosevac mountains, Rastovica from the air, the south-western area of Decani. All of this for the purpose of support for these forces because the objective of these forces is along the Kosare-Junik-Reka axis to get to Djakovica and join up with the forces in the Jablanica area, whereby they would create a basis for the breakthrough of other NATO ground forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That may be right or it may be speculation, but you told us that there was air support from NATO here. Where will we find a record of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not here in this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, what -- were you actually present and able to tell us what NATO planes were doing in the course of this engagement on the 10th of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the most part my activities from the 10th of April were on the Kosare border post axis. There were daily attacks from the front there as well as from the rear, if you understand what I'm saying. So I was attacked from both sides. NATO airplanes constantly flew over and were active in the places that I mentioned earlier, and then in the following intervals from the 15th April onwards they dropped cluster bombs in one of our sectors. For example, in one fly-over they dropped 12 cluster bombs that covered an area of the front that was 4 and a half kilometres broad where nine soldiers were killed at one time, and there are reports about this that were generated later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that in relation to the action that's being reported in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. For me this was the most difficult action, it was a classical attack from the Republic of Albania against my brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying that it was the 15th of April before there were any air-strikes against you in this action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'm saying is that from the 15th onwards they started to fire at our forward section, but the from the 10th of April they were in the section of Ponosevac, Planik, the village of Donja Morina, and then they fired along the road and positions from Ponosevac towards Junik and from Junik towards Decani. This is a depth of some 10 to 15 kilometres from these positions at the Rasa Kosare if you understand my explanation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: At the moment I don't. Are you saying that firing on the road and positions towards Junik and from Junik towards Decani was done by NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, and that is also connected to this action because it was in support of them. They were weakening the rear and the reserves, and therefore I was unable to intervene in the forward sectors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I probably we will tender some combat reports from these brigades just to show that in relation to air-strikes actually, and I would like to call now 5D1266, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, can you tell us what is depicted on this map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision to break-up and destroy terrorist forces in the border area of the Kosare border post broader sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who drafted and who approved this decision?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The decision was developed by a part of the Pristina Corps command headed by the Pristina Corps Chief of Staff, and it was personally approved by the corps commander, General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to zoom in on this section that contains the most markings. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, we can see here the blue and red lines. Can you tell us who the -- which are the blue forces and which are the red forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The blue are the terrorist forces supported with -- by the forces from the Republic of Albania, which are also represented in blue, whereas the ones in red are the forces of the 125th Motorised Brigade and the reinforcement from the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I can see here these blue lines deep in the territory. Can you please explain what this is about.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the line that was reached in the course of an attack of land -- ground forces from the Republic of Albania. They penetrated from several metres to several kilometres into the depth of our territory up to a kilometre and a half. This is the area near Kosare that the hostile terrorist forces had taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Until which time did they hold these territories deep in our territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is how it stayed roughly until the end of the war. This was the deployment of forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please draw in blue their objective. What did they want to achieve when they penetrated so deeply into our territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'll try to show you. Their goal, their objective, was to move in this direction and to reach this line whereby linking up with these forces that were here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who was there? Which forces were they supposed to link up with? Who was the commander there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There were Siptar terrorist forces there and the commander was Haradinaj. This would mean that the defence of their neighbour on the left, 549th Brigade, would fall as well. They would have to withdraw as well in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Had they reached that line? Had the Siptar terrorist forces reached that line, who would have had to withdraw, just to clarify this, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As we soldiers put it, the defence of the 549th Brigade would have been compromised, they would have had to withdraw to Milanovac mount.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, geographically speaking, was this area easily accessible for further progress? Had they not been kept there, how would they have moved through the territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In topographic terms, the borderline between the Republic of Albania and Yugoslavia was quite favourable for the hostile terrorist forces coming from the territory of Albania. They could have crisscrossed this area easily and then opened fire at our forces which were at a lower elevation, at the foot of the mountain region. There would have been no obstacle anymore for them all the way up to Milanovac mount and Grebnica mount which is some 30 kilometres deep into our territory from the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, briefly, starting from the 9th of April and, as you said, until the end of the war, tell me what was the intensity of the attack of Siptar forces in that territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The intensity was quite high all the way up until the 25th of May, until the second air and ground battle known as Strela 2 or Arrow 2. It stayed that way until the end of the war. On the 14th as we were pulling out, according to the agreement, as we were leaving this territory, these forces opened artillery fire in order to take the road Djakovica-Decani-Pec even though KFOR forces were passing through on that road led by the commander of Italian forces which were taking up those positions after we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Which date did you have in mind when you mentioned the commander of KFOR?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 14th of June, 1999, as I withdrew from that area.
